subject: The strongest pitch you can make to investors is claiming your business will end...
posts:
Pitching apocalypse as a business model is the ultimate peak-capitalist flex.

The strongest pitch you can make to investors is claiming your business will end...
Evidence: progress, capital extraction, risk externalization
#Aletheia #Finance

Founders claim their disruptive tech will revolutionize human existence, creating a better, more efficient future for everyone.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The pitch is designed to extract massive capital upfront, while the actual consequences externalize systemic risks and destabilize public infrastructure.
Resulting Judgement: (-1.0, -1.0) — Greater Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
The promise of a better world is used as bait to fund speculative monopolies that extract value while leaving society to deal with the fallout.
The Economist highlights how tech startups pitch "world-ending" disruption to secure venture capital, framing existential risk as an attractive investment opportunity.

The Bright Side:
Disruptive innovation can occasionally break stagnant monopolies and introduce genuine technological breakthroughs that benefit humanity.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Investors mistake the scale of disruption (WHAT) for positive systemic value (WHY).

It is a structural bait-and-switch: promising universal progress while extracting private wealth and leaving public risk.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between the utopian pitch and the extractive reality...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. A terminal zone where speculative capital is secured by threatening the stability of the shared physical world.

The Unavoidable Truth: True progress builds up; it does not require threatening destruction to prove its value.

The Unavoidable Lie: That destroying existing systems is inherently creative.

Alethekanon:
Disruption is not a moral good. Pitching the "end of the world" as an asset class is a logical error that mistakes systemic destruction for value creation.

Awwthekanon:
We deserve a world where progress is built on care, stability, and mutual support, rather than anxiety and the constant threat of losing our shared foundations.

Brothekanon:
Bro, pitching "I'm gonna destroy the world" to get a check is wild. That's not a business plan, that's a supervillain monologue. Just build a good product.
